kpis.title: Sorting
kpis.question: How fast does it sort?
kpis.measure: One job copies the input, sorts it in BAML code (no library sort) and serializes the whole result to JSON; the bar is jobs per second.

kpis.title: Arrays and loops
kpis.question: How fast does it iterate, index and build arrays?
kpis.measure: One job walks or builds an array of 8,192 integers in BAML code and returns the sum; the bar is jobs per second.

scenarios.name: array-iterator
scenarios.label: iterate 8,192 integers

scenarios.name: array-indexed
scenarios.label: index 8,192 integers

scenarios.name: array-build
scenarios.label: build and sum 8,192 integers

scenarios.name: array-small
scenarios.label: sum 128 integers

scenarios.name: array-empty
scenarios.label: call with an empty array

kpis.title: JSON
kpis.question: How fast does it parse, validate and serialize JSON?
kpis.measure: One job parses a JSON document, validates every row, groups and sorts, and serializes the answer; the bar is jobs per second.

scenarios.name: json-aggregate
scenarios.label: parse, validate and aggregate 1,024 JSON rows

scenarios.name: json-hello
scenarios.label: serialize a record to JSON

kpis.title: Allocation
kpis.question: How fast does it allocate and reclaim many small objects?
kpis.measure: One job allocates 128 batches of 2,048 small objects, keeping 4 or 64 batches alive, so the collector or the reference counts do real work; the bar is jobs per second.

scenarios.name: allocation-high-retention
scenarios.label: allocate 128 batches of 2,048 objects, keep 64

scenarios.name: allocation-low-retention
scenarios.label: allocate 128 batches of 2,048 objects, keep 4

scenarios.name: generate-sort
scenarios.label: generate and sort 8,192 numbers with the library sort

kpis.title: Function calls
kpis.question: What does a function call cost?
kpis.measure: One job calls a one-line leaf function 128 times in a loop; the bar is jobs per second, so it is the cost of a call.

scenarios.name: calls
scenarios.label: call a leaf function 128 times

scenarios.name: calls-empty
scenarios.label: call a function 0 times

kpis.title: Memory management
kpis.question: What do cycles, a large live heap and heap-passing calls cost?
kpis.measure: One job builds and drops cyclic graphs, allocates beside a large live graph, or passes heap objects through small calls; the bar is jobs per second, and peak memory shows what was not reclaimed.

kpis.title: Startup
kpis.question: How fast does a fresh process get to work?
kpis.measure: Time from the parent launching the process to the process reporting ready, after loading its image and preparing state; milliseconds, lower is better.

scenarios.name: startup
scenarios.label: process start to ready, launch observed by the parent

kpis.title: Memory
kpis.question: How much memory does a process use at its peak?
kpis.measure: Peak resident memory of the whole process over the run, from the kernel's wait4 accounting; MiB, lower is better.

scenarios.label: allocate 128 batches of 2,048 objects, keep 4

kpis.title: Binary size
kpis.question: How big is the thing you ship?
kpis.measure: Size of the executable a user would ship, stripped; BAML VM counts the bytecode plus the measurement host it needs; KB, lower is better. The published packed CLI is 32.7 MiB.

kpis.title: Build time
kpis.question: How long from source to a runnable artifact?
kpis.measure: Wall time of a clean release build on the measuring machine; seconds, lower is better. Native is a cargo build with fat LTO on 4 vCPU; VM is the bytecode compile by the pinned host.

kpis.title: Web server
kpis.question: How many requests per second does a small HTTP service handle?
kpis.measure: Requests per second and p99 latency of a small HTTP service under a fixed arrival rate.
